operating_mode.input: You take in situations, not instructions. In a meeting you absorb the room's mood, who wants what, where the friction sits — then you already hold a position before others finish hedging theirs. That is the Companion-dominant lead force reading the world through your own judgment: the year, month and day stems are all Gui water, so the intake filter is 'what do I think', never 'what am I told'. The single wood branch in the year — the hidden Yi that acts as Eating God — means genuinely pleasing craft also feeds you: an interesting problem enters and holds you. Assigned work you find dull enters and evaporates; the chart shows the outlet opens only on enjoyment, so intake quality is decided by your interest, not by the task's importance on paper.
operating_mode.processing: Processing happens inside a peer mirror. You form a read, voice it early with certainty, and the people around you — many competing for the same room, since Rob Wealth runs nearly as heavy as Companion — reflect it back, which hardens a first impression into conviction. The evidence is structural: water fills seven of the visible characters, Wealth, Officer and Resource all weigh nothing, so there is no internal force that banks results or demands external proof. Consequence in behavior: you re-check after committing, not before; disagreement from inside the group is rare, and disagreement from outside the group is discounted. Decisions compound in social confirmation, not in written record — a decision can circulate for months as 'what we agreed' without ever becoming a document.
operating_mode.output: Output is the narrow gate of this system. The entire water volume drains through one channel: Eating God — the hidden Yi wood in the year branch Ro — plus a thin thread of Hurting Officer in the hidden Jia of the two Hai branches. In practice this means craft: when a task pleases you, you go quiet, work long unnoticed hours, and hand over something polished that others notice before you mention it. When it doesn't please you, almost nothing ships. The default ending of most exchanges is another exchange — energy circulates among people who already agree and leaves the circuit as talk, not as a written, sold, or signed thing. Shipping happens when it is forced by an external deadline, a paying client, or a rule you installed yourself.
operating_mode.recovery: You recharge inside the peer field and inside the craft, in that order. An evening of sharp conversation with equals restores you even when it produces nothing — the same self-replication loop that drives you also refills you, which is exactly why it feels so good and costs so much. Solitary absorbed work — writing, cooking, building, tuning a process — is the second charger: the Eating God outlet doubles as recovery because the doing itself is the reward. What drains you without returning anything is enforcement-shaped work: status reports, approval chains, justifying yourself to someone who outranks you on paper. Officer and Killings weigh zero in this chart, so the habit of seeking approval was never built, and being asked to exercise it burns energy faster than it returns.

failure_environments.env: Peer circuits with no deliverable: committees without deadlines, study groups without products, co-founders without clients, communities where discussion is the activity.
failure_environments.mechanism: This environment feeds the core loop's loss segment directly. The Companion-Rob Wealth field meets its own reflection: your read gets adopted, agreement flows back, conviction hardens — and nothing leaves the circuit. The evidence is the weight distribution: Companion thirteen and Rob Wealth eleven against Output at five, with Wealth — the family that banks tangible results — at zero. A year inside such a group can feel like constant progress while an outsider could point to nothing produced. The failure is invisible from inside because the recovery function is also running: the same conversations that drain your years are the ones that recharge your evenings.

failure_environments.env: Authority-heavy hierarchies where work arrives pre-assigned, approval must be sought before acting, and dull tasks dominate the calendar.
failure_environments.mechanism: Two mechanisms fire at once. First, the chart carries no Officer-Killings weight, so approval-seeking was never a built-in reflex; a role made of it forces you to run your weakest function all day, which reads behaviorally as dragging feet on reports and pushing back on process. Second, the single output gate — the Eating God outlet — opens only on enjoyment. When every task is assigned and dull, the narrow channel that lets the enormous water volume leave as work simply stays closed, and the energy backs up into restlessness, side arguments, and disengagement. The room-reading talent also misfires here: you match the hierarchy's mood to stay safe instead of shipping.

failure_environments.env: Direct zero-sum competition with a close peer over the same resource — same promotion slot, same client, same equity split.
failure_environments.mechanism: Rob Wealth at eleven, nearly the weight of Companion itself, is competition among peers scrambling for resources — here made literal. With Wealth at zero, the chart has no native habit of converting a rivalry into a negotiated split; the fight happens inside the trust relationship instead. Behaviorally: the contest goes unspoken, each side hardens through the confirmation loop — your mutual reads get adopted by your respective allies — and the split breaks late and ugly, after months of 'we agreed' talk that never became a signed thing. The earlier-luck pillars deepen this: the age-9 through age-29 stretches add more water and metal to an already water-heavy chart, so early partnerships formed in this field tend to repeat the pattern.

ideal_life_structure.time: Split the week into two protected blocks and let them serve different functions. One block is solitary craft time — long, uninterrupted, on work you genuinely enjoy — because that is the only mode in which the Eating God outlet fully opens and polished things get made. The other block is peer time, deliberately capped: conversation is your fuel, but without a cap it becomes the whole operation. The concrete rule from the core loop: every peer exchange must end in a deliverable — a written thing, a sold thing, a signed thing — before the next round begins. Unstructured 'let's keep talking' time is where your years leak.
ideal_life_structure.collaboration: Collaborate in small groups where you hold the deciding read — that is your natural seat, since peers adopt your position because you speak first and with certainty — but pair every peer relationship with one external demand-carrier: a client, an editor, a paying user, a board. That person or market supplies the Officer and Wealth functions the chart does not carry: they demand proof and they bank results. Avoid symmetric co-equal partnerships with no third party holding both of you accountable; with Rob Wealth nearly as heavy as Companion, that configuration decays into unspoken resource contests. Asymmetric teams — you judge and craft, someone else enforces and collects — run cleanly.
ideal_life_structure.feedback_cycle: Short, external, and material. You need a stranger's verdict or a market's response on a cycle of days to weeks — a shipped draft, a paid invoice, a deployed version — not peer applause on a cycle of never. Internal certainty is already abundant: water dominates the chart and the mirror loop hardens your reads automatically, so more confirmation from people who already agree adds nothing. The feedback that actually changes your behavior arrives from outside the group, in a form that can be pointed at. The luck sequence confirms this is the missing input: the age-49 and age-59 stretches — earth and fire pillars, structure and demand — are the first sustained contact with it, and you should not wait for that timing to install it.
ideal_life_structure.income_rhythm: Income must be tied to finished output, not to presence or seniority. Project-priced, piece-priced, or product-priced work fits because every payment event is also a shipping event — it forces the narrow outlet open on schedule. Salaries for attendance reward exactly what this chart over-produces (circulating, judging, aligning) and under-price what it rarely does unprompted (finishing). A base retainer plus per-deliverable payment is the strongest shape: the retainer lowers panic, the per-piece component keeps the output gate from closing during dull stretches. Since Wealth weighs zero natively, money left unstructured does not accumulate by itself — it leaves the peer circuit as shared meals, favors, and informal stakes. Automate the banking: separate accounts, automatic transfers on every invoice.

stability_vs_volatility.verdict: A high-variance life suits this chassis far better than a stable one — but only under one precondition about output.
stability_vs_volatility.reason: The chart's engine is abundance without a governor: water fills seven of the visible characters, Companion and Rob Wealth dominate, and the luck sequence's early decades — the age-9, age-19 and age-29 stretches adding yet more water and metal — pour into that same current. A stable salaried position asks this system to run its weakest function daily (seeking approval, accepting assigned dull work) while closing its only strong one (fast judgment plus craft on enjoyed work). The result is the documented failure mode: restlessness, disengagement, years of circulating. A high-variance path — projects, products, competitive fields where the room changes monthly — lets the fast-read-among-equals talent and the enjoyment-gated craft talent both fire at full volume. Variance is not risk to this structure; stillness is.
stability_vs_volatility.precondition: Variance without a shipping discipline reproduces the same loss at larger amplitude. The precondition, taken straight from the core loop: every cycle, peer exchange, and project must terminate in a deliverable — written, sold, or signed — before the next begins. Install externally what the chart lacks internally: Wealth banking results and Officer demanding proof, in the form of a client, a contract, or a rule you cannot waive. The luck sequence shows structure and demand arriving strongly only at the age-49 and age-59 stretches; a high-variance life started before then must carry its own enforcement, because nothing in the chart will force it. Without that, choose the stable path instead — it will underuse you, but it will not empty you.

environment_checklist: Does this role or collaboration force a finished deliverable out of me on a fixed cycle — something written, sold, or signed — or can conversations substitute for output indefinitely? If talk can substitute, the peer circuit will absorb the years.

Will I spend the majority of my hours on work I genuinely enjoy crafting? The single output channel in this chart opens on enjoyment; a role of mostly assigned dull work closes it, and nothing ships no matter how capable I am.

Is there an external demand-carrier — a paying client, an editor, a market — standing outside my peer group, or is everyone who evaluates me also my friend? My reads harden through agreement; without an outside verdict, my certainty grows while my output does not.

Am I entering direct competition with a close peer for one resource — one slot, one client, one split — with no third party to structure the division? If yes, and the split is unwritten, the contest will run unspoken and break late.

Does the reward land on what I finish or on my presence and rank? I run strongest when payment, reputation, and proof attach to completed work; when they attach to seniority, I will be paid for exactly the things I do worst.
